title: Automation and modulation share an explicit base-vs-offset contract

needles: A route is not an automation lane
a modulation route is authored and rewired in place and removed whole
a stale route expectation is refused
keeps dense modulation out of legacy param events
base and offset remain one canonical automation value
dense modulation delivery refuses queue overflow explicitly
dense modulation ordering survives the sample-rate and block matrix

installed_sdk.rationale: The public state and timeline headers expose the canonical base-vs-offset value, route validation, and bounded dense queue.

offline_timeline_cli.rationale: The timeline model preserves routes, but no offline CLI operation publishes this packet's complete base-vs-offset and dense-delivery contract yet. Typed deferred receipt: status=deferred, code=UnsupportedSurface, operation=automation.modulation.route, required=route lifecycle plus dense overflow receipt.

offline_timeline_mcp.rationale: No offline MCP operation currently preserves dense route delivery and typed refusal results end to end. Typed deferred receipt: status=deferred, code=UnsupportedSurface, operation=automation.modulation.route, required=route lifecycle plus dense overflow receipt.

live_product_control.rationale: The approved minimal installable DSPX-04 example host owns a prepared Processor SignalGraph, binds the canonical resolver, and proves the insert, rewire, and remove lifecycle for the prepared graph route through the broker. The generic CLI and generated MCP projections reach the same registry operation. This promotes live control for the namespaced example host only; Forge and commercial products still require their own equivalent receipt.

design_time_agent_manifest.rationale: The installed agent manifest already exposes the canonical dense Processor modulation capability; this packet aligns its base-vs-offset and refusal semantics with the public state contract.

needles: Graph-owned Processor nodes receive bounded borrowed dense modulation lanes
